title: Cross-lingual Robustness of Behavioral Coordination Signals for Detecting State-Linked Information Operations
abstract_or_snippet: Tests whether behavioral-coordination detection signals (used to flag CIB) hold up across languages for state-linked operations.
why_relevant: Q5/Q7: directly relevant to the brief's point that CIB detection is the wrong tool for a network whose baseline behavior IS the content-farm norm — this paper's cross-lingual robustness testing is the technical detail behind that limitation.
search_query: platform coordinated inauthentic behaviour detection account provenance policy
gate_reason: quality_floor:suspect_venue — hosted on scipublication.com (generic OJS 3.4.0.9 instance, journal titled 'Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Review'), with internally inconsistent Dublin Core metadata (DC.Date.created 2025-07-13, but DC.Date.dateSubmitted 2026-06-28 — submitted AFTER the issued date of 2025-07-01, and modified 2026-06-28). Unfamiliar DOI prefix (10.69987) with no independent verification of peer-review rigor. The paper's content is also suspiciously precisely tailored to this project's own search-query wording (5 named canonical coordination signals, exact concept_target G phrasing) — a pattern consistent with AI-generated content-mill output rather than independently conducted research. Declining rather than risk citing a paper-mill result for a specific empirical claim (cross-lingual detection generalization) the Drafter would otherwise treat as settled science.
